texts.at-0001: Round money only with round_money Always round monetary Decimal results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
texts.at-0002: Normalize money inputs with to_money before storing Convert any incoming amount to Decimal via `to_money` from `ledgerly.money` before comparing or storing it on models; compare against `ZERO` from the same module.
texts.at-0003: Raise BillingError with snake_case codes and str payload Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with a snake_case code (e.g. `invalid_state`, `negative_amount`) and the offending value stringified as the detail.
texts.at-0004: Exclude bool when validating integer arguments When validating an `int` parameter, reject `bool` explicitly first (`isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)`) since `True`/`False` pass `isinstance(..., int)`.
texts.at-0005: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc before arithmetic In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc` before doing arithmetic or comparisons (see `ledgerly/subscriptions.py:current_period`); never compare raw datetimes directly.

item.title: Raise BillingError with snake_case codes
item.content: Invalid billing input must raise `BillingError` from `ledgerly.errors` with a short snake_case code (e.g. "invalid_tax_rate") and the offending value as the second argument, not ValueError.
